proof: DIFFERENT UNIT: the headroom category is a property of a (layout, team_size) cell; the Recoverability label is a property of a (decision event, candidate topology) pair.

DIFFERENT INITIAL CONDITION: headroom is evaluated from the nominal scenario initial condition; Recoverability is evaluated from a realized state at control step t>0 selected by REALIZED_TRAJECTORY_UNIFORM_K.

DIFFERENT POLICY CLASS: headroom qualification runs always COMPACT, always LINE and the scripted oracle; Recoverability source states are reached under S0-S5, of which S3, S4 and S5 are not fixed-topology.
DIFFERENT TEMPORAL SCOPE: headroom asks whether a topology held for the whole episode completes the task; Recoverability asks whether committing to a topology from this state completes the remainder.
NO SHARED CODE PATH: the recoverability generator, acquisition and compiler never read a headroom category.

C28_h2_protection.statement: H2 is neither weakened nor strengthened by this audit. Its family eligibility comes from the measured headroom requalification, which this phase leaves untouched.

binding.why: H2 is scoped to 'predeclared families with genuine topology headroom'; that phrase is the scenario headroom category

binding.object: candidate commitment at one realized decision state

hypotheses.H1: Recoverability selection improves episode task success by at least 0.08 absolute over both direct classification and local geometric selection, while meeting the frozen collision gate.
hypotheses.H2: Online COMPACT/LINE reconfiguration improves episode task success by at least 0.10 absolute over each fixed topology in predeclared families with genuine topology headroom.
hypotheses.H3: The decentralized full method retains at least 0.85 of centralized diagnostic task success, with collision-free degradation no greater than 0.01.
